newsitem.title: CHINA: HK shares score record close, Hutchison leads.
newsitem.headline: HK shares score record close, Hutchison leads.

text.p: Hong Kong shares ended at a record closing high on Tuesday with virtually all market attention focused on blue-chip conglomerate Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, which continued a record-breaking rally.
The Hang Seng Index gained 105.47 points, or 0.67 percent, to close at 15,772.06, beating its previous all-time closing high of 15,738.81 points hit on July 23.
Market turnover reached HK$17.60 billion compared with HK$16.90 billion on Monday.
Hutchison closed the session up HK$3.00 at HK$74.75 after hitting a record high at HK$75.00 and was the most actively traded issues in value terms.
Traders said heightened hopes that Hutchison will strike telecommunications deals in China had given the shares a push.
"The market is really excited about these deals," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP-PrimeEast Securities.
Brokers said they had re-rated the stock.
Lennon Chan Wing Luk, executive director at Tai Fook Securities, characterized the day's trading as a "little bit artificial."
"People are trying to push up the (cash market) price to settle," Chan said, referring to the upcoming expiry of July Hang Seng Index futures on Wednesday.
Ahead of futures settlement and a batch of U.S. economic data due later this week, the market has stayed range-bound, he added.
July Hang Seng Index futures rose 70 to 15,750, and August contracts gained 90 to 15,820.
Investors confident in HSBC Holdings' long-term prospects drove the stock HK$2.00 higher to HK$261.00 ahead of the bank's interim results due to be released next week.

Meanwhile, traders said a Hong Kong Monetary Authority statement, made Monday, was "an excuse" to push property shares higher. HKMA said a further tightening of mortgage lending did not seem necessary at this time.
Cheung Kong Holdings added HK$1.50 to HK$78.00, and New World Development gained HK$2.00 to HK$52.75.
